[nation]Cordone[/nation]]October, 2004
Karyatsh Border
The border between Pantagruel and Karyatsh was one of immense military presence. The United nations recently instituted a United Nations mandated DMZ between the two states to keep peace, their efforts were far and varied. Almost 15,000 U.N. Peacekeepers were statioend across the border of Pantagruel. These divisions would be highly equipped to make sure the malevolent Ganbataar Dynasty didnt question the sovereignty of Karyatsh. But little did they know, these efforts were in vain, Ganbataar was to rule Amarallo.

September, 2006
Grand Superion Batzorig Ganbataar recently ordered his latest Military exercise across the DMZ. Batzorig has only been in power for a mere 6 years after the unfortunate death of his father, Genghis Ganbataar. Batzorig had ambitions for expanding the Pantagrueli borderlands across Amarallo to continue the Imperial Ambition of the Ganbataar dynasty. On september 27th, 2004, Batzorig would enforce a national General Mobilization, increasing the Pantagrueli forces across the DMZ from 5,000 to over 55,000 in a matter of a few days. These actions wouldnt go unnoticed by the U.N. who would sanction the Ganbataar dynasty and enforce multiple embargoes on the state. This did little to wane the ambitions of Batzorig. As the mobilizations would continue to ramp up more and more.

November 4th, 2006
2 Weeks before the Invasion
The Pantagruelian defense ministry would host multiple plans on how to commit a swift invasion of the Kartyashi state, operations in Kartyash would be kept modest and below the radar as of this time as multiple Pantagrueli spies would be funneled through the state. These spies would begin to collect information on Kartyashi military installations and government positions. Sabatoge missions would also take place, multiple radar stations would be tampered with unknown to the Kartyashi administration. 

November 10th, 2006
8 Days before the Invasion
Pantagrueli forces would begin re-activating multiple dormant tunnel systems leading straight to the Kartyashi capital across the border. Meanwhile, Kartyashi forces would recieve warnings from the U.N. of an impending Pantagrueli invasion, U.N. forces would be placed on high alert while Kartyashi forces would be strongly urged to open arms. But these warnings from the U.N. would come to deaf ears, as the Kartyashi administration would seek no effort in increasing its security if an impending Pantagrueli invasion was to come. This would only aid their doom, the Kartyashi administration would instead send a strongly worded letter to the Ganbataar dynasty requesting they reconcile back to the 2004 division. But they would never receive a response from the Pantagruelians, this would cause mild worry across the Kartyashi government but would not be taken into serious consideration.

November 17th, 2006
One Day before the start of the invasion
By midnight, Pantagrueli strategic forces would open fire on a Kartyashi civilian airliner, crashing it and resulting in the deaths of over 201 persons. But the terror wouldnt end there, the Kartyashi sky would be filled with hundreds of Ground-to-Ground missiles, meanwhile, hundreds of towed-batterys would open fire on the D.M.Z. catching both U.N. and Kartyashi forces off gaurd. In the skies, multiple Mig-29s would enter the aerospace of the Kartyashi administration and begin striking both civilian and military targets. These attacks would prove extremley succesful and catastrophic towards the Kartyashi people. Thousands of sleeping civillians would be caught in the cross-fire leading to the highest number of Civilian fatalities in a single hour of Kartyashi history. 

November 18th, 2006
The day of the invasion.
With both U.N. and Kartyashi forces in despair, the ground invasion of Kartyash would commence. A combined mechanized and motorized force of over 65,000 ground-troops would cross into the D.M.Z., U.N. forces would try to resist the invading masses but these efforts would come to no avail. In hours, U.N. peace-keeping forces would officially withdraw from Kartyash. WIth no available aid from the U.N, Kartyashi forces would be forced to retreat from the border. These un-organized retreats would result in heavy Kartyashi casualties on all fronts.

November, 22nd, 2006
4 Days after the invasion
Pantagruelian forces would continue to push Kartyashi retreating forces. With heavy air superiority and naval dominance, Pantagrueli forces would be able to seize the Kartyashi capital with little to no resistance. But as the Pantagruelians continued advancing, the slower their gains were. Until the front began to stabilize in the favor of the Kartyashis. This was dismal to the Pantagrueli forces who hoped for a swift take over of Kartyash. And soon Kartyash forces began even making a counter-offensive. As a last-resort to keeping the offensive fluctuating Pantagrueli forces ordered a Artillery-Mass of over 800 Towed-Batteries. This plan would prove effective in bogging down Kartyashi forces and forcing a major retreat and allowing for Pantagruel to take the coast.

December 16th, 2006. 
28 days after the invasion.
Routed and destroyed, the Kartyashi army would enforce an unconditional surrender without government approval.  With the uncondtiional surrender it would bring end to the 1 month war, Kartyash would be forced to concede most of its lands to Pantagruel and sign a treaty becoming a premanently neutral buffer state.
[/spoiler]

[spoiler= The Siege of Peace] winds of the North Sea are howling through the Thule Bay crashing into the cliffs of Sverker Bay, carrying the silent rumors of ambition and need for change.In the south, the lands of Kønugard are found and are a distant dream of Jomsland. For many years the Commonwealth had watched these territories from across the bay, knowing that they were once a part of their great nation. It was december in the year 2020 when the Nirnir began weaving the string of fate in Jomslands favor.High King Leif V. stood before the Jarls of Jomsland, his voice as steady as the fires of Muspelheim. Our people have always thrived by uniting our scattered legacy, he spoke, his eyes burning with determination. Our old lands call to us.Not as raiders or conqueros, but as rebuilders and as unifiers.
The Siege of Peace in late december of the same year marked the first step. Civil war had erupted in Kønugard, the fracturing government unable to contain the tides of chaos at bay. Jomsland, observing the situation decided to help the civilians.Soldiers marched into the land delivering food and medicine to destroyed settlements.Engineers repaired roads and bridges so the civilians could be safely evacuated.
Among these brave engineers was Erik Halvorsson, a young man from Warångia who grew up listening to the mystical stories of the first commonwealth.As he stood on the crumbling remains of an old highway, leading to an abandoned village, he felt the weight of ancient history pressing down on him. we are not just rebuilding the roads. he said to on of his coworkers. We are rebuilding an ancient connection.
But not everyone felt the same.Other nations of Elseyr accused Jomsland of exploiting Kønugards vulnerability and instability for their own gain. Humanitarian Imperialism they called it, their accusations carried across the continent by diplomatic envoys.Internally whispers of doubt began to spread through Jomsland.
The High King, however didnt gave up. He met these doubts with actions instead of trying to to kill the doubt off with speeches.Over the next years, Jomsland heavily invested into Kønugard, building ports, schools and hospitals.What once had been a war ravaged land was now pulsing with life.The Doubters grew quieter and were replaced with Optimists supporting the cause.By the year 2023 the bond between Jomsland and Kønugard had grown stronger but a full integration remained a dream for the future.It was High King Jorik III. who made the dream a reality.He was a visionaryleader who knew that Kønugard would not be taken.It had to be welcomed. Let the people decide, he said his voice echoing through Bondahall. Let them choose their future. In 2024 a referendum was held in Kønugard. Erik Halvorsson, now a father and community leader in a coastal village watched as his neighbors lined up to cast their votes. He thought of the stories his grandmother told him and the years of rebuilding this once war ravaged country. The Gods truly have blessed us. he whispered to his infant daughter who clutched his hand tightly.The results were clear. 72 % of the population voted in favor of joining the second commonwealth of Jomsland. On a cold december morning in 2024, Kønugard officialy became part of the commonwealth.Celebrations started in the entire country, from the gigantic port of Marskborg to the quiet fishing villages of Sverker Bay. Fireworks lighting up the night sky, their reflections coloring the big icebergs of North Sea. But Kønugard joining the commonwealth was not the end of the voyage.The following days were littered with challenges and difficulties.Differences in Culture that arose from the years of isolation from one another, surface like spiky rocks beneath calm waters. For example in one village where almost a fight broke out due to a local festival clashing with jomslandic traditions, which sparked a heated debate about national identity and culture. Surprisingly these moments of conflict lead to unity being forged. Erik, sadly terminal ill with cancer, continued to speak at regional meetings, urging patience and tolerance. We are not trying to erase your past and culture. he often said. We are trying to weave it into something new.Today, Kønugard shows what can be achieved through perserverance and vision. The newly built LNG facilities hum with activity, powering most of the country and even making enough to be sold to other nations. The ports once withered and broken now bustle with trade, their docks filled with exotic and expensive wares from all of Erene.And in the hearts of the people, a sense of newfound national pride has taken root, deep and indestructible. Sadly Erik Halvorsson lost his battle against cancer and entered Valhalla, but his legacy lives on. In the small coastal village he lived in for the past 4 years, a silver statue of him stands beside the newly built Halvorsson Community Center his gaze fixed towards the city of Marskborg.Beneath it, a plaque reads: To those who build bridges where others see walls.[/spoiler]
